mainTopic: How long a boy and a girl take to form in the womb (רבי ישמעאל against the חכמים), and רבי שמלאי's אגדה about the baby's life in the womb.
overview: The גמרא finishes asking why the משנה makes a woman with an unidentified miscarriage count like a mother of a boy and of a girl, when she already keeps the rules of נדה. It answers with cases of blood on day 34 and day 41, and on day 74 and day 81, where those counts make her wait longer. Next it turns to רבי ישמעאל, who holds that a boy is formed in 41 days and a girl only in 81. The חכמים reject his comparison from the days of impurity, and the גמרא shows that his real proof is the extra word תֵּלֵד said about a girl. Two versions of a story about קליאופטרא's experiment on her maidservants are told, and each side calls the other's proof one 'from fools.' The גמרא then explains why the משנה repeats the view of the חכמים: so we do not rule like רבי ישמעאל just because the פסוקים seem to support him. The amud ends with רבי שמלאי's אגדה about the baby in the womb: how it lies, how it eats, how it learns the whole תורה, how it forgets it at birth, and the oath it swears to keep its נשמה pure. A new statement by רבי אלעזר begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why mention the boy-birth rules if she already keeps נדה rules?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה: it already says she keeps the rules of נדה, so what does 'she counts as a mother of a boy' add?
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה already teaches that she keeps the rules of נדה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends its question. The משנה already made her keep the rules of נדה, so adding the rules of a mother of a boy seems to change nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the rules of נדה, every time she sees blood she is impure. That is already stricter than the 'days of purity' of a mother of a boy. So it seems the boy-birth rule could never make her stricter than she already is.

keyTerms.meaning: But it already teaches! (a challenge from the wording of the משנה)
A woman made impure by her monthly bleeding, who is impure for seven days

phrases.english: But it teaches 'a menstruating woman'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the question begun just before this section of text, about the משנה's rule that she counts like a mother of a boy.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a woman with an unidentified miscarriage counts like a mother of a זכר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rules of נדה are always at least as strict, so the boy-birth rule seems to add nothing.

steps.title: Blood on day 34 and again on day 41
steps.stepSummary: The boy-birth rule matters when she sees blood on day 34 and again on day 41: she stays forbidden until day 48.
steps.simpleTranslation: It matters for this case: if she sees blood on day 34 and sees blood again on day 41, she stays 'spoiled' until day 48.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a case where the boy-birth rule makes her wait longer than the rules of נדה alone would.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood on day 34 makes her a נדה for days 34 to 40. Under נדה rules alone, blood on day 41 would need only a short one-day wait. But if the baby was a boy, her days of purity ended on day 40. So day 41 begins a fresh seven days of נדה, and she must wait until day 48.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Spoiled', meaning she stays forbidden to her husband

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think day 41 is impure only because of the boy rule. Without it she would still be careful for one day. The boy rule makes it a full new seven-day count, so she waits until day 48.

phrases.english: That if she sees blood on the thirty-fourth day,
and she sees again on the forty-first day,
she is 'spoiled' until the forty-eighth day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a practical case where the rule makes a difference
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The boy-birth rule never makes her stricter than the rules of נדה.
steps.terutzMaskana: When blood comes on day 34 and again on day 41, the boy rule makes day 41 the start of a new seven-day count, until day 48.

steps.title: The matching case for a girl: day 74 and day 81
steps.stepSummary: The girl-birth rule matters the same way: blood on day 74 and again on day 81 keeps her forbidden until day 88.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same goes for the rule of a mother of a girl: if she sees blood on day 74 and again on day 81, she stays 'spoiled' until day 88.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the girl-birth rule also adds something real, with the same kind of case at different numbers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood on day 74 makes her a נדה for days 74 to 80. Under נדה rules alone, day 81 would need only a short wait. But if the baby was a girl, her days of purity lasted until day 80. So day 81 begins a fresh seven-day count, and she waits until day 88.

keyTerms.meaning: And the same with regard to
A female: here, the rules of a woman who gave birth to a girl

steps.whatToRemember: Each extra rule (boy, girl, נדה) can add its own stringency. Day 41 matters for a boy and day 81 matters for a girl, because each starts a new seven days of נדה right after the days of purity end.

phrases.english: And similarly with regard to a female:
that if she sees blood on the seventy-fourth day,
and she sees again on the eighty-first day,
she is 'spoiled' until the eighty-eighth day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same answer as step 2 for the girl-birth rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The girl-birth rule makes day 81 the start of a new seven-day count, until day 88.

steps.title: The משנה quotes רבי ישמעאל on day 41
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: רבי ישמעאל says that a miscarriage on day 41 counts like a boy and like a נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says: on the forty-first day, she counts like a mother of a boy and like a נדה, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new part of the משנה, the opinion of רבי ישמעאל. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל holds that a male fetus is formed by day 41 but a female fetus only by day 81. So a miscarriage on day 41 could be a formed boy, but not a formed girl, and the girl-birth rule does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: She 'sits', meaning she keeps the counting and rules of
A male: here, the rules of a woman who gave birth to a boy
Etc.: the quote from the משנה continues

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר: יוֹם אַרְבָּעִים וְאֶחָד
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael says: on the forty-first day,
phrases.notes: This means a woman who miscarried on day 41 after she went to the מקוה.

phrases.english: she sits as for a male and as a menstruating woman, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר: יוֹם אַרְבָּעִים וְאֶחָד תֵּשֵׁב לְזָכָר וּלְנִדָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: רבי ישמעאל's opinion in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A miscarriage on day 41 makes her keep the rules of a boy-mother and of a נדה, but not those of a girl-mother.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל's source: the תורה treats boy and girl differently
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings רבי ישמעאל's reasoning: the תורה gives different impure and pure days for a boy and for a girl.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי ישמעאל says: for a boy the תורה made her impure and then pure, and for a girl it made her impure and then pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי ישמעאל begins to explain where his opinion comes from. The next step finishes his explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a boy, the פסוק gives 7 impure days and 33 pure days, 40 in all. For a girl it gives 14 impure days and 66 pure days, 80 in all. רבי ישמעאל will use these different totals to show that a boy and a girl take different amounts of time to form.

keyTerms.meaning: He (the תורה) made her impure and made her pure: her days of impurity and days of purity

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for רבי ישמעאל's view that a boy is formed in 41 days and a girl in 81 days.

phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yishmael says:
He deemed impure and deemed pure with a male,
phrases.notes: 'He' means the תורה. See ויקרא 12:2–4: seven impure days, then thirty-three pure days.

phrases.english: and deemed impure and deemed pure with a female.
phrases.notes: See ויקרא 12:5: fourteen impure days, then sixty-six pure days.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר: טִימֵּא וְטִיהֵר בְּזָכָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source behind רבי ישמעאל's ruling in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תורה gives a boy-mother and a girl-mother different periods of impurity and purity. This is the start of רבי ישמעאל's proof.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל's comparison: the impurity days match the formation days
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל argues that the 40 days of טומאה and טהרה for a boy match the 40 days a boy takes to form. So the 80 days for a girl must match 80 days for a girl to form.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as for a boy, the time the תורה makes her impure and then pure matches the time the boy takes to form, so too for a girl, the time the תורה makes her impure and then pure matches the time the girl takes to form.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues רבי ישמעאל's argument from Step 5. He draws a parallel between the impurity count and the time it takes the baby to form.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a boy, the mother has 7 impure days plus 33 pure days, a total of 40, and a boy is formed in about 40 days. רבי ישמעאל says the girl must follow the same pattern: 14 plus 66 is 80, so a girl is only fully formed after 80 days. That is why a miscarriage on day 41 can only be treated as a boy.

keyTerms.meaning: The formation of the baby in the womb
The תורה made her impure, then pure (the days of impurity followed by the days of purity)
Matching it, the same as it

phrases.english: Just as when it made her impure and pure for a male,
its formation matches it,
phrases.notes: For a boy: 7 impure days plus 33 pure days makes 40, the same as the time a boy takes to form.

phrases.english: so too when it made her impure and pure for a female,
its formation matches it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה כְּשֶׁטִּימֵּא וְטִיהֵר בְּזָכָר יְצִירָתוֹ כְּיוֹצֵא בוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the reasoning that the ברייתא began in Step 5
steps.raayaObject: רבי ישמעאל's view that a girl is formed only after 80 days
steps.raayaSupportSource: The parallel between the 40/80 days of impurity and purity in ויקרא 12 and the formation time

steps.title: The חכמים reject learning formation from impurity
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that the length of a baby's formation cannot be learned from the length of the mother's impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: We do not learn the formation of a baby from the rules of impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים reject רבי ישמעאל's comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים say these are two separate topics. How many days the mother is impure is a halachic rule, and it does not tell us how long the baby takes to form. So the 80 days for a girl prove nothing about her formation.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not learn (one thing from another)

phrases.english: They said to him:
One does not learn formation from impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אֵין לְמֵדִין יְצִירָה מִטּוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison made in Step 6
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole comparison between impurity days and formation days
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Impurity rules are a separate topic and cannot tell us how a baby develops

steps.title: The חכמים bring the story of קליאופטרא
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים bring a story: קליאופטרא examined her maidservants who were sentenced to death and found that both boys and girls were formed by day 41.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to רבי ישמעאל: There was a story with קליאופטרא, queen of Alexandria. Her maidservants were sentenced to death by the government. She examined them and found that both, boy and girl, were formed by day 41.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים add a factual proof against רבי ישמעאל from something that was actually observed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This attacks רבי ישמעאל directly. If a girl embryo is also fully formed by day 41, then a miscarriage on day 41 could be a girl. That would mean the woman should count the days for a girl too.

keyTerms.meaning: A story, an incident that happened
A death sentence from the government

phrases.english: They said to Rabbi Yishmael:
There was an incident with Cleopatra, queen of Alexandria,
whose maidservants were sentenced to death by the government,
and she examined them and found them,
phrases.notes: She checked the embryos of her pregnant maidservants to see how far along they were.

phrases.english: both this one and that one, on the forty-first day!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ לְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: מַעֲשֶׂה בִּקְלֵיאוֹפַּטְרָא מַלְכַּת אֲלֶכְּסַנְדְּרוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second argument against רבי ישמעאל, this time from observation
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's claim that a girl is not formed until day 81
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An observed case showed that girls, like boys, are formed by day 41

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל dismisses the קליאופטרא proof
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל answers that he is bringing a proof from the תורה, while they are bringing one from fools.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I bring you a proof from the תורה, and you bring me a proof from fools?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל rejects the story of קליאופטרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not accept the observation as reliable, and he calls the people involved fools. For him, a proof from the תורה is stronger than a report like this. This also raises a question: what exactly is his proof from the תורה?

phrases.english: He said to them:

phrases.aramaic: אֲנִי מֵבִיא לָכֶם רְאָיָיה מִן הַתּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: I bring you a proof from the Torah,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַתֶּם מְבִיאִין לִי רְאָיָיה מִן הַשּׁוֹטִים?!
phrases.english: and you bring me a proof from fools?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: אֲנִי מֵבִיא לָכֶם רְאָיָיה מִן הַתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קליאופטרא story from Step 8
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the קליאופטרא story
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It comes from unreliable people, and a proof from the תורה outweighs it

steps.title: What is רבי ישמעאל's proof from the תורה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what proof from the תורה רבי ישמעאל means. It cannot be the 40/80 comparison, because the חכמים already rejected it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the proof from the תורה? If you say it is the comparison: the תורה made her impure and pure for a boy, and impure and pure for a girl, and so on. But they already told him: you cannot learn formation from impurity!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא itself now speaks. It challenges רבי ישמעאל's claim to have a proof from the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only proof we have seen so far is the comparison in Step 6. But the חכמים knocked it down in Step 7. So how can רבי ישמעאל still call it a proof from the תורה? He must have a different source.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (the גמרא suggests an answer in order to reject it)
But look, didn't... (points to a problem)
We do not derive (the same as אֵין לְמֵדִין)

phrases.english: What is the proof from the Torah?
If you say: it made her impure and pure for a male,
and it made her impure and pure for a female, etc.
phrases.notes: כּוּ׳ means 'and so on.' The גמרא is pointing back to the full argument from Step 6.

phrases.english: But they already said to him:
One does not derive formation from impurity!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the 'proof from the תורה' that רבי ישמעאל mentioned in Step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's statement that he has a proof from the תורה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The only proof we know of, the 40/80 comparison, was already rejected by the חכמים, so it cannot be his strong proof

steps.title: The extra word תֵּלֵד for a girl
steps.stepSummary: The real proof is the word תֵּלֵד. The תורה adds another mention of birth for a girl, which shows a girl has a separate, longer timeline.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'תֵּלֵד' (she gives birth). The תורה added another mention of birth for a girl.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 10 by showing רבי ישמעאל's real proof, taken from an extra word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק already mentioned birth for a boy, so it could have simply said 'and if it is a girl.' Instead it repeats the word תֵּלֵד. רבי ישמעאל learns from this that a girl's formation is its own separate 'birth' process, which takes twice as long. This is a direct reading of a word in the פסוק, so the objection 'you cannot learn formation from impurity' no longer applies.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק added (an extra word that teaches something)
Another birth, a separate mention of giving birth

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל's source is not the 40/80 comparison, which was rejected. It is the extra word תֵּלֵד said about a girl. That is why he holds that a miscarriage on day 41 can only be a boy.
steps.whyThisMatters: This keeps רבי ישמעאל's ruling standing: a miscarriage on day 41 is treated only as a boy, because a girl is not yet formed then.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'she gives birth,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 12:5

phrases.english: the verse added for her
another birth in the case of a female.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 10 by giving רבי ישמעאל's real source
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a different source: an extra word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: His proof was the 40/80 comparison, which the חכמים rejected
steps.terutzMaskana: His proof is the extra word תֵּלֵד, which teaches that a girl has a separate formation timeline

steps.title: Why the experiment is a proof from fools: the girl may have started earlier
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי ישמעאל calls the קליאופטרא experiment foolish. It answers that the girl-baby's mother may have become pregnant 40 days before the boy-baby's mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why is it a proof from fools? Say that the female was conceived first, 40 days before the male.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what was wrong with the חכמים' proof from קליאופטרא. It answers that the experiment had a hole in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים claimed both a boy and a girl were formed by day 41. רבי ישמעאל says the girl's mother might have conceived 40 days before the experiment started. If so, the girl really took 80 days to form, which fits his view.

phrases.english: And what is the 'proof from the fools'?
phrases.notes: This goes back to רבי ישמעאל's words in step 9.

phrases.english: Say: the female came first,
and was conceived forty days before the male.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains רבי ישמעאל's dismissal from step 9
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is wrong with the קליאופטרא proof
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The female pregnancy may have begun 40 days earlier, so the girl really took 80 days

steps.title: The חכמים reply: she gave them a drug to clear out any earlier pregnancy
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that קליאופטרא gave the maidservants a drug to drink, so no one could have been pregnant before the experiment.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים? She gave them a purging drug to drink.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back against רבי ישמעאל's objection. They say an earlier pregnancy was ruled out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קליאופטרא gave the women a drug that would end any pregnancy before the test began. So every pregnancy started at the same time, and the 'she started earlier' idea fails.

keyTerms.meaning: That shakes out, a purging drug

phrases.english: And the Rabbis? She gave them a purging drug to drink.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the 'earlier pregnancy' objection of step 12
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the female pregnancy started first
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A purging drug would have ended any earlier pregnancy

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: some bodies are not affected by the drug
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל answers that the drug does not work on every body, so an earlier pregnancy could still have survived.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ישמעאל? There are bodies that do not react to the drug.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל defends his objection against the חכמים' reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The drug is not a guarantee. If the girl's mother was one of the women it did not affect, her pregnancy may have started 40 days earlier. Then the experiment proves nothing.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yishmael?
There is a body that does not take in the drug.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אִיכָּא גּוּפָא דְּלָא מְקַבֵּל סַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the חכמים' drug argument from step 13
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the drug ruled out an earlier pregnancy
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The drug does not work on everyone

steps.title: Second version: רבי ישמעאל brings the קליאופטרא story as his proof
steps.stepSummary: In another ברייתא, רבי ישמעאל uses the קליאופטרא story. Here she found a boy formed at 41 days and a girl at 81 days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל said to them: There was a story with קליאופטרא, queen of the Greeks. Her maidservants were sentenced to death by the government. She examined them and found a male formed at 41 days and a female at 81 days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of the argument. This time the קליאופטרא experiment supports רבי ישמעאל's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this telling, the results match רבי ישמעאל exactly. A boy forms in 40 days and a girl in 80 days, with the extra day each time.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with step 8! There, the חכמים told the קליאופטרא story to prove both form at 41 days. Here, in a second version, רבי ישמעאל tells it with different results to support himself.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael said to them:
There was an incident with Cleopatra, queen of the Greeks,
whose maidservants were sentenced to death by the government,
and she examined them and found
a male formed at forty-one days,
and a female at eighty-one days.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל מַעֲשֶׂה בִּקְלֵפַּטְרָא מַלְכַּת יְוָונִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second version of the debate in which the sides are switched
steps.raayaObject: רבי ישמעאל's view that a male forms in 41 days and a female in 81
steps.raayaSupportSource: קליאופטרא's examination of her condemned maidservants

steps.title: The חכמים: we don't bring proof from fools
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים dismiss רבי ישמעאל's story as a proof from fools.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: We do not bring a proof from fools.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים reject the קליאופטרא proof. In this version they are the ones using the 'fools' line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same charge רבי ישמעאל made in step 9 ('you bring me a proof from fools'), but now the חכמים make it. The next step explains what flaw they see.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not bring a proof

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אֵין מְבִיאִין רְאָיָה מִן הַשּׁוֹטִים.
phrases.english: They said to him: One does not bring proof from the fools.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 15
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The קליאופטרא story as proof for רבי ישמעאל
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The experiment is unreliable (explained in the next step)

steps.title: Why it is foolish: the girl's mother may have conceived 40 days late
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the flaw the חכמים see: the girl's mother may have waited 40 days before she actually became pregnant.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? The one with the female waited forty days, and only then became pregnant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the חכמים call this version of the experiment foolish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the mirror image of step 12. There, the girl's pregnancy might have started 40 days early. Here, it might have started 40 days late. Either way, the girl may really have formed in 40 days, just like the boy.
steps.whatToRemember: In both versions, the experiment can be knocked down by doubting when the pregnancy really began. That doubt is why each side calls the other's proof 'from fools'.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
That one with the female remained forty days,
phrases.notes: Literally 'was left over.' She didn't conceive right away, so the count started 40 days too early.

phrases.english: and then became pregnant.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא הָךְ דִּנְקֵבָה אִיַּיתַּרָה אַרְבְּעִין יוֹמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the dismissal in step 16
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the חכמים call the proof foolish
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The female's mother may have conceived 40 days late, so the girl really took only 40 days

steps.title: The maidservants were under a guard
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל defends his proof: the maidservants were handed to a guard, so none of them could have become pregnant later.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ישמעאל? He would say: they were handed over to a guard.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל answers the flaw raised in Step 17, that the girl's mother may have become pregnant later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים said the girl's mother may have waited 40 days before she became pregnant. רבי ישמעאל replies that a guard watched the maidservants the whole time. So no later pregnancy was possible, and the 81-day count stands.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yishmael (how would he answer)?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking how רבי ישמעאל would answer the problem from Step 17.

phrases.english: She handed them over to a guard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the חכמים's flaw from Step 17
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the girl's mother became pregnant late
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The חכמים ignored that the maidservants were watched by a guard

steps.title: A guard cannot be trusted with עריות
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reply that no guard can be relied on in matters of forbidden relations. The guard himself may have been with her.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים? There is no guardian for forbidden relations. Say that the guard himself was with her.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on רבי ישמעאל's guard answer, so the doubt about a later pregnancy returns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים use a known rule: in matters of עריות, no guard can be fully trusted. The guard himself could have made her pregnant later. So the girl's 81 days may really have been fewer, and the proof falls.

keyTerms.meaning: no guardian can be relied on in matters of forbidden relations

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule אין אפוטרופוס לעריות is a well-known principle that shows up elsewhere in הלכה.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis (how would they answer)?
There is no guardian for forbidden relations,
say that the guard himself had relations with her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי ישמעאל's defense in Step 18
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the guard as proof that there was no later pregnancy
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A guard cannot be relied on in matters of עריות, and he himself might be the cause

steps.title: Maybe the girl was already formed at 41 days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי ישמעאל's proof: if they had checked the girl at 41 days, maybe she would already have been formed like the boy.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe, if they had opened up the woman with the girl on day 41, she would have been found formed like the boy?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem with the proof itself. Finding the girl formed at 81 days does not show she was not already formed earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The experiment only showed that the girl was formed by day 81. Nobody checked her on day 41. So maybe girls are also formed by 41 days, and the experiment proves nothing about a difference.

phrases.english: But perhaps:
if they had cut open the one with the girl
on day forty-one,
she would have been found (formed) like the boy?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִילְמָא אִי קַרְעוּהוּ לְהָךְ דִּנְקֵבָה בְּאַרְבְּעִין וְחַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new attack on רבי ישמעאל's proof from Step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's proof that a girl is formed only at 81 days
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being formed at 81 days does not rule out being formed already at 41 days

steps.title: The signs of growth were the same
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the girl at 81 days and the boy at 41 days showed the same signs of growth. So the girl took twice as long to reach the same stage.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: their signs were the same.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends רבי ישמעאל's proof against the question in Step 20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The girl at 81 days looked exactly as developed as the boy at 41 days. If she had been formed at 41 days, she would have looked more developed by day 81. So she must have only just been formed.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
In their signs they were the same.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 20
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The girl might have been formed already at 41 days
steps.terutzMaskana: Equal signs of growth show the girl was only just formed at 81 days
steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל's proof stands against this question because the girl at 81 days matched the boy at 41 days.

steps.title: Why does the משנה repeat the view of the חכמים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the חכמים in the משנה and asks: they say the same thing as the תנא קמא, so why repeat it?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: both the forming of a boy and the forming of a girl, etc. But the חכמים are the same as the תנא קמא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and points out what looks like an extra line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה already treats 41 days as the point for both boys and girls. The חכמים at the end say the same thing. So the גמרא asks why the משנה needs to say it twice.

keyTerms.meaning: the first, unnamed opinion in the משנה

phrases.english: And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד בְּרִיַּית זָכָר וְאֶחָד בְּרִיַּית נְקֵבָה וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Both the forming of a male and the forming of a female, etc.
The Sages are the same as the first Tanna!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the experiment debate and turns to the wording of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The repeated opinion of the חכמים in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two opinions that say the same thing make the second one look unneeded

steps.title: It cannot be just to show the הלכה follows the majority
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the repeat shows the first opinion belongs to the many חכמים, so the הלכה follows it. It rejects this, because that is already obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say it is to show that the unnamed first part follows the חכמים, and between one and many the הלכה follows the many, that is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer to Step 22 and then knocks it down. The next step gives the real answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One could think the משנה repeats the view to show that many חכמים hold it against רבי ישמעאל alone. But everyone already knows that the הלכה follows the many against one person. So that cannot be the reason for the extra line.

keyTerms.meaning: to make (the opinion) unnamed, as the plain teaching
between one Sage and many, the הלכה follows the many

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the rule of following the many is wrong. It only says the rule is so well known that the משנה would not need extra words to teach it.

phrases.english: And if you will say
(it comes) to make the first clause the plain teaching, like the Rabbis,
and (between) an individual and many, the halakha follows the many,
that is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests and rejects a possible answer to Step 22
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the repeat only shows the הלכה follows the majority
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The rule יחיד ורבים הלכה כרבים is already obvious, so it needs no extra line in the משנה

steps.title: The repeat is needed because רבי ישמעאל's view looks convincing
steps.stepSummary: The משנה repeats the חכמים so that we do not rule like רבי ישמעאל just because the פסוקים seem to support him.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: רבי ישמעאל's reasoning makes sense, since the verses support him. So the משנה teaches us that the majority holds otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its real answer to why the משנה repeats the opinion of the חכמים. The repeat tells us that the הלכה goes like the majority, even against an argument that looks strong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 23 the גמרא said that 'the הלכה follows the majority' is obvious. Here it explains why it is not so obvious in this case. רבי ישמעאל has פסוקים that seem to back him up, so we might have ruled like him. The repeated line in the משנה shows that the majority disagrees, so the הלכה stays with them.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought (introduces a mistaken idea the text comes to block)
It teaches us (tells us what we would not have known)

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים are repeated in the משנה to show that the הלכה follows the majority, even though רבי ישמעאל's view seems to have support from the פסוקים.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying רבי ישמעאל is wrong about the פסוקים. It is saying that even a well-supported opinion does not win against the majority.

phrases.english: Lest you say:
Rabbi Yishmael's reasoning makes sense,
since the verses support him,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean 'support him.'

phrases.english: so it teaches us.
phrases.notes: It teaches us that most of the חכמים hold the first opinion, so we do not rule like רבי ישמעאל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the real answer after the first suggestion was rejected in step 23
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why something that seems obvious needed to be taught (מהו דתימא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the פסוקים support רבי ישמעאל, maybe the הלכה follows him even though he is outnumbered
steps.terutzMaskana: The repeat of the חכמים shows that the majority disagrees, so the הלכה follows them

steps.title: How a baby lies folded in the womb
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמלאי compares the baby in the womb to a folded notebook and describes its body position.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמלאי taught: What is a baby in its mother's womb like? Like a folded notebook. Its hands rest on its temples, its arms on its knees, and its heels on its buttocks. Its head rests between its knees. Its mouth is closed and its navel is open.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic, an אגדה from רבי שמלאי about life inside the womb. He describes how the baby is curled up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects to the topic of the daf, which is how a baby forms in the womb. The picture is of a body folded tightly, like the pages of a closed notebook. He points out that the mouth is closed and the navel is open, which sets up the next step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Simlai taught:
What is a baby in its mother's womb like?
Like a folded notebook,
and its hands rest on its two temples,
its two arms on its two knees,
and its two heels on its two buttocks,
and its head rests between its knees,
and its mouth is closed, and its navel is open.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new אגדה topic about the baby in the womb
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the womb the baby lies folded up, with its mouth closed and its navel open

steps.title: How the baby eats, and what changes at birth
steps.stepSummary: The baby eats and drinks from what its mother takes in. At birth its mouth opens and its navel closes.
steps.simpleTranslation: It eats from what its mother eats and drinks from what its mother drinks. It does not release waste, so that it will not kill its mother. Once it comes out into the world, the closed part opens and the open part closes. Otherwise it could not live even one hour.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמלאי continues. He explains how the baby is fed in the womb and what happens to its body at birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on the last line of step 25, where the mouth was closed and the navel open. Inside the womb the baby is fed through its navel. At birth the two switch, so the mouth opens and the navel closes, and the baby must now eat by mouth.

keyTerms.meaning: The air of the world (being born)

phrases.english: And it eats from what its mother eats,
and it drinks from what its mother drinks,
and it does not release waste
so that it will not kill its mother.
And once it comes out into the air of the world,
the closed opens, and the open closes,
phrases.notes: The closed part is the mouth and the open part is the navel, as in the end of step 25.

phrases.english: for if not for this,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לִחְיוֹת אֲפִילּוּ שָׁעָה אַחַת.
phrases.english: it could not live even one hour.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי שמלאי's description and explains the closed mouth and open navel
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The baby is fed through its mother in the womb, and at birth its mouth opens and its navel closes

steps.title: A light over the baby's head lets it see the whole world
steps.stepSummary: A light burns over the baby's head and it sees from one end of the world to the other. The proof is a פסוק in איוב, and dreams show that this is possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: A light burns over its head, and it looks and sees from one end of the world to the other. As it says: 'When His lamp shone over my head, by His light I walked through darkness.' Do not be surprised, because a person can sleep here and see a dream in Spain.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמלאי adds that the unborn baby has a special light and can see the whole world. He brings a פסוק as a source and then explains why this is not so strange.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of a lamp over the head that lights up the darkness, and he reads it as the dark womb. To show that seeing very far away is possible, he compares it to a dream. A sleeping person can see faraway places in a dream.

phrases.english: And a light burns for it over its head,

phrases.aramaic: וְצוֹפֶה וּמַבִּיט מִסּוֹף הָעוֹלָם וְעַד סוֹפוֹ,
phrases.english: and it looks and gazes from one end of the world to the other,
as it says:
"When His lamp shone over my head,
phrases.notes: איוב 29:3

phrases.english: by His light I walked through darkness,"
and do not be surprised,
for a person can sleep here
and see a dream in Spain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another detail to רבי שמלאי's description of the baby in the womb
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The unborn baby has a light over its head and sees the whole world, based on איוב 29:3

steps.title: The womb is the happiest time of a person's life
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמלאי says no days are as good for a person as the months in the womb, and he brings a פסוק from איוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are no days when a person is better off than those days, as it says: 'If only I were as in the months of old, as in the days when God watched over me.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמלאי says that a person is never better off than in the womb. He quotes the פסוק just before the one in step 27.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איוב wishes to return to 'months of old' when God guarded him. רבי שמלאי reads this as a wish to be back in the womb. The next step proves that the פסוק really means the womb.

keyTerms.meaning: Living in a good, blessed state

phrases.english: And there are no days

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאָדָם שָׁרוּי בְּטוֹבָה יוֹתֵר מֵאוֹתָן הַיָּמִים,
phrases.english: when a person lives in more goodness than those days,
phrases.notes: 'Those days' are the months the baby spends in the womb.

phrases.english: as it says:
"If only I were as in the months of old,
phrases.notes: איוב 29:2

phrases.english: as in the days when God watched over me,"

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לְךָ יָמִים שֶׁאָדָם שָׁרוּי בְּטוֹבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי שמלאי's teaching with the פסוק just before the one in step 27
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The months in the womb are the best time of a person's life

steps.title: Proof that the פסוק means the months of pregnancy
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק counts in months, not years, and the only time of life counted only in months is pregnancy.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which days have months but no years? You must say: these are the months of pregnancy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמלאי proves that the פסוק in step 28 is about the womb. He looks closely at the word 'months.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: איוב said 'months of old,' not 'years of old.' Any long time of life would be counted in years. Pregnancy is the one stage that lasts only months, never a full year, so the פסוק must be about the womb.

keyTerms.meaning: You must say (the only possible answer)
The months of pregnancy before birth

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמלאי's whole teaching shows the womb as a protected, blessed place where the baby is fed, sees the world, and is guarded by God.

phrases.english: And which are the days

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם יְרָחִים וְאֵין בָּהֶם שָׁנִים?
phrases.english: that have months but do not have years?
You must say:
these are the months of pregnancy.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵיזֶהוּ יָמִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם יְרָחִים וְאֵין בָּהֶם שָׁנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves that the פסוק quoted in step 28 refers to pregnancy
steps.raayaObject: That 'months of old' in איוב 29:2 refers to the time in the womb
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק uses 'months' and not 'years,' and only pregnancy is counted in months without years

steps.title: The baby is taught the whole תורה in the womb
steps.stepSummary: The baby in the womb is taught the entire תורה. Two פסוקים are brought as proof, one from משלי and one from איוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the baby is taught the whole תורה, as it says: "And He taught me and said to me: Let your heart hold fast My words; keep My commandments and live." And it also says: "When the secret counsel of God was upon my tent."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמלאי continues his teaching and adds one more good thing that happens in the womb: the baby learns the entire תורה. He brings two פסוקים to prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the list of the good things that happen in the womb from the earlier steps. The first פסוק talks about being taught God's words. The second פסוק, from איוב, describes a time when God's secret counsel was 'upon my tent.' The גמרא will soon explain why it needs both.

keyTerms.meaning: "And it also says": a signal that a second פסוק is being brought

phrases.english: And they teach it the entire Torah,
as it says: "And He taught me and said to me:
phrases.notes: משלי 4:4

phrases.english: Let your heart hold fast My words;
keep My commandments and live."
And it also says: "When the secret counsel of God was upon my tent."
phrases.notes: איוב 29:4

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another feature of the baby's life in the womb to רבי שמלאי's description.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The baby in the womb is taught the entire תורה.

steps.title: Why bring a second verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why it needed to add the second פסוק from איוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the point of "and it also says"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask why a second פסוק was needed when one was already given. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally one good proof is enough. When the גמרא adds 'וְאוֹמֵר,' it is a sign that the first proof has a weakness. The question asks what that weakness is.

phrases.english: What is the point of "and it also says"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the need for the second proof-text brought in step 30.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why both פסוקים are needed to show the baby learns תורה in the womb.

steps.title: The first verse might be only about a prophet
steps.stepSummary: The first פסוק is spoken by a נביא, so you might think only a prophet learns תורה in the womb. The second פסוק shows it is true for every person.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say that it is a prophet who is speaking, and maybe this only applies to him, come and hear: "When the secret counsel of God was upon my tent."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the first פסוק could be read as being only about the prophet who said it. The second פסוק shows that this happens to everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The weakness in the משלי פסוק is that a נביא is the speaker, and a נביא is special. So we could not prove from it that ordinary people learn תורה in the womb. The פסוק in איוב closes that gap and teaches that this is true of every baby.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say: introduces a possible objection

steps.whatToRemember: Every baby, not only a prophet, learns the whole תורה in the womb. That is why the גמרא brings two פסוקים.

phrases.english: And if you would say: it is a prophet who is saying this,
come and hear: "When the secret counsel of God was upon my tent."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משלי פסוק might apply only to a נביא; the איוב פסוק shows it applies to everyone.

steps.title: At birth an angel makes the baby forget the תורה
steps.stepSummary: When the baby comes out into the world, an angel slaps it on the mouth and it forgets the whole תורה. The proof is a פסוק in בראשית.
steps.simpleTranslation: And once the baby comes out into the air of the world, an angel comes and slaps it on its mouth and makes it forget the whole תורה, as it says: "Sin crouches at the opening."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמלאי's teaching goes on to the moment of birth: an angel slaps the baby's mouth and all the תורה it learned is forgotten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the turning point from the womb to the world. The proof פסוק speaks of sin waiting 'at the opening.' Here that means the moment of birth: once the baby forgets its תורה, sin is already waiting for it.

keyTerms.meaning: The air of the world, meaning being born

phrases.english: And once it comes out into the air of the world,
an angel comes and slaps it on its mouth,
and makes it forget the entire Torah,
as it says: "Sin crouches at the opening."
phrases.notes: בראשית 4:7. The "opening" is the moment of birth; once the תורה is forgotten, sin is right there waiting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the תורה learned in the womb to its being forgotten at birth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At birth an angel slaps the baby and it forgets the whole תורה.

steps.title: The baby must swear an oath before being born
steps.stepSummary: The baby is not born until it is made to swear an oath. The proof is a פסוק in ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it does not come out from there until they make it swear an oath, as it says: "That to Me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds that before the baby leaves the womb, it is made to take an oath. It quotes a פסוק, and the next step will explain how this פסוק proves it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new detail about the time just before birth. The words 'every tongue shall swear' are the key to the proof. The גמרא will explain them in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: They make him swear an oath

phrases.english: And it does not come out from there
until they make it swear an oath,
as it says: "That to Me every knee shall bow,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 45:23

phrases.english: every tongue shall swear."

steps.title: Explaining the verse: bowing is death, swearing is birth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the two halves of the ישעיהו פסוק. 'Every knee shall bow' is the day of death, and 'every tongue shall swear' is the day of birth. Each half is backed up by a פסוק from תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: "That to Me every knee shall bow": this is the day of death, as it says: "All who go down to the dust shall kneel before Him." "Every tongue shall swear": this is the day of birth, as it says: "He who has clean hands and a pure heart, who has not taken My name in vain, and has not sworn deceitfully."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how the ישעיהו פסוק proves the oath at birth. It splits the פסוק into two parts and connects each part to a different day in a person's life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bowing is tied to death through a פסוק that speaks of those who 'go down to the dust' kneeling. Swearing is tied to birth through a פסוק praising the person who 'has not sworn deceitfully,' meaning he kept the oath he swore before he was born. So the swearing in ישעיהו is the oath taken at birth.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who go down to the dust, meaning the dead

steps.whatToRemember: Every person swears an oath before birth. A good person is one who keeps it and does not swear 'deceitfully.'

steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 34 told us an oath exists but gave none of its content. This question asks for the wording.

steps.title: The words of the oath: be righteous and keep your soul pure
steps.stepSummary: The oath is to be a צדיק and not a רשע, to see yourself as a רשע even if everyone praises you, and to keep your pure נשמה pure, or it will be taken away.
steps.simpleTranslation: Be a צדיק and don't be a רשע. Even if the whole world tells you that you are a צדיק, see yourself as a רשע. Know that הקב"ה is pure, His servants are pure, and the soul He gave you is pure. If you keep it pure, good. If not, I will take it from you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the wording of the oath. It has two parts: how to see yourself, and a warning to keep your נשמה pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part warns against relying on other people's praise. Even a person everyone calls a צדיק should not feel sure of himself. The second part says the נשמה comes from a pure source and is given on a condition: keep it pure, or it is taken back.
steps.confusionAlert: 'See yourself as a רשע' does not mean to think you are worthless. It means you should never feel so sure you are a צדיק that you stop being careful.

phrases.english: Be righteous and do not be wicked,
and even if the whole entire world
says to you, "You are righteous" —
be in your own eyes like a wicked person.

phrases.aramaic: וֶהֱוֵי יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא טָהוֹר,
phrases.english: And know that the Holy One, Blessed be He, is pure,
and His servants are pure,
and the soul that He put in you is pure.
If you guard it in purity — good,
and if not — I will take it from you.
phrases.notes: The 'I' here is the one giving the oath, the angel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 36 by giving the oath's wording.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The oath: be a צדיק, see yourself as a רשע even when praised, and keep your pure נשמה pure, or it will be taken away.
steps.whatToRemember: Every person swears before birth to be a צדיק, to stay humble about his own goodness, and to keep his pure נשמה pure.

steps.title: Parable of the כהן who gives תרומה to an עם הארץ
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל compares the soul to תרומה that a כהן gives to an עם הארץ, warning him to keep it pure or it will be burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: It is like a כהן who handed תרומה to an עם הארץ and told him: If you keep it pure, good. If not, I will burn it in front of you.
steps.whatsHappening: The school of רבי ישמעאל gives a parable to explain the warning at the end of the oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן is like הקב"ה, the תרומה is like the pure נשמה, and the עם הארץ is the person, who may not be careful with purity. Ruined תרומה is burned, and in the same way a נשמה that is not kept pure is taken back. This makes clear that the נשמה is not ours to do with as we like. We are holding something holy that we must guard.

keyTerms.meaning: the holy portion of produce given to a כהן, which must be kept pure
a person not careful about the laws of purity
burning it (what is done to תרומה that became impure)

steps.whyThisMatters: In הלכה, תרומה that becomes impure may not be eaten and must be burned. The parable uses this rule to show how serious it is to keep the נשמה pure.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
A parable: to a priest who handed over teruma
to an am ha'aretz, and said to him:
phrases.notes: An עם הארץ here is someone who isn't careful about purity, so he might let the תרומה become impure.

phrases.english: If you guard it in purity — good,
and if not — I will burn it in front of you.
